title: Shillong, Kaziranga and Tawang (Batch 5)
selection: Batch 5. Shillong (4 sections), Kaziranga (5, two of them state-level filler) and Tawang (3) get who it's for, best time, food, shopping, practical info, things to do, culture, common mistakes and FAQs, plus fuller overviews (pending review). Kaziranga's filler practical_info and things_to_do get replacement suggestions. Itineraries (meghalaya-4-days, assam-5-days, tawang-6-days) are left for the itinerary audit. Not covered: safari fees, permit fees, current safari booking rules.

places.seoTitle: Shillong Travel Guide: Lakes, Falls & Viewpoints
places.seoDescription: Plan Shillong: Shillong Peak, Ward's Lake, Elephant Falls, the Don Bosco Museum, Umiam Lake, Laitlum and day trips to Mawlynnong and Kongthong.

images.alt: View over Shillong city in the hills

overview.text:
Shillong, Meghalaya's hill capital, was capital of undivided Assam until 1972. Its colonial bungalows, churches and pine-covered hills earned it the name 'Scotland of the East', and it is also India's self-styled 'Rock Capital', with live music in cafes across town. The city takes its name from Lei Shyllong, the deity believed to live on Shillong Peak.

The Peak, at 1,966 m and 10 km out, is the state's highest point, and Elephant Falls drops in three tiers 12 km away. In town are Ward's Lake and the Don Bosco Museum of Northeast cultures. Umiam Lake is on the road from Guwahati, 100 km and about 2.5 hours away. Shillong is the base for Laitlum, the Mawphlang sacred grove, the 16 km David Scott Trail and the villages of Mawlynnong and Kongthong. Visit September to May.

images.alt: Grassland and trees in Kaziranga National Park

overview.text:
Kaziranga, on the south bank of the Brahmaputra, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and home to two-thirds of the world's one-horned rhinos, 2,401 at the last count, as well as the largest populations of wild water buffalo and eastern swamp deer. Protection began after Lady Curzon's visit in 1904, and it became a Tiger Reserve in 2007.

The park runs about 40 km east to west across tall elephant grass, marshes and shallow pools, with the Karbi Anglong hills and tea gardens to the south. You see it by jeep or elephant safari through its ranges, from Kohora in the centre to Bagori in the west and Agaratoli in the east; hiking is not allowed. It is about two hours from Tezpur. In July and August the monsoon floods most of the western park.

places.name: Tawang
places.summary: A Monpa town at about 3,000 m around India's largest monastery.
places.seoTitle: Tawang Travel Guide: Monastery, Sela & War Memorials
places.seoDescription: Plan Tawang: Tawang Monastery, the War Memorial, Jaswant Garh, Sela Pass, Nuranang Falls, and the Inner Line Permit.

overview.text:
Tawang sits at about 3,000 m in western Arunachal Pradesh, about 555 km from Guwahati, and is home to the Monpa people. Its monastery, Gaden Namgyal Lhatse, founded in 1680–81, is the largest in India, with around 450 monks; the 14th Dalai Lama stayed here after crossing into India in 1959.

The road in crosses Sela Pass at 4,170 m, now bypassed by the all-weather Sela Tunnel, past Jaswant Garh, where Jaswant Singh Rawat held off the Chinese army for 72 hours in 1962. Around town are the Tawang War Memorial and Nuranang Falls, which drop over 100 m. Snow falls every December–January. Indian visitors need an Inner Line Permit, and foreigners a Protected Area Permit.

how_to_reach.text: Fly to Guwahati (about 555 km) or Tezpur (about 320 km), then drive over Sela Pass or through the Sela Tunnel.

best_time.text: Snow falls every December–January, when the town has a ski lift but Sela Pass can close after heavy snow; the tunnel keeps the road open. Landslides can close the pass in other seasons too.
